transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m just tired all the time. I mean, I’m a teacher, so I know what normal end-of-the-day tired feels like, but this is different. Even when I get a full night’s sleep, I still feel like I have to push myself through grading, making dinner, and getting ready for the next morning.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Yes… most days, I think. I can still smile and be upbeat with my students and get through the lessons, but underneath I feel kind of gray and flat. Then I come home and that feeling is still there, and things I usually enjoy, like my garden or watercolors, just feel distant somehow.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been a little over two years now… about two years and two months. I think it started around when my husband stopped working outside the home and our household routine changed.
Have you had any periods in the past two years where you felt completely back to normal, without these gray and flat feelings?

No, not really. It’s been pretty steady since it started—about two years and two months ago, when my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine changed. I might have better days, but I don’t think I’ve felt completely back to normal in that time.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yes… I think so. I still do things sometimes, but they don’t feel the same. My garden and my watercolors used to feel relaxing, but lately they just feel kind of far away, like I can’t really connect with them. I can get through the day and smile for my students, but underneath it’s just this gray, flat feeling that follows me home.
Are these gray and flat feelings something you experience for most of the day?

Yes… I’d say most of the day, most days. I can still smile for my students and get through my lessons, but underneath there’s usually that gray, flat feeling. It tends to come home with me too, and even things like my garden or watercolors feel kind of distant.
Have you had these gray and flat feelings for most of the day, every day, for the entire two years and two months?

Most days, yes. I can still put on a smile at school and get through my lessons, but underneath it’s usually there—that gray, flat feeling. It follows me home, too, and even things like my garden or watercolors just feel kind of far away.
Do you still enjoy things you used to, or has your pleasure in them decreased?

Yes, it’s decreased. I still try to do those things—like gardening or painting—but they don’t really feel enjoyable the way they used to. It’s like I’m doing them from a distance, with that gray, flat feeling still there.
Have you ever had a period where these gray and flat feelings went away completely, only to come back later?

No, not really. It’s been pretty steady since it started, about two years and two months ago, around when my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine changed. I might have better days, but it hasn’t fully gone away and then come back.
Has anything significant changed in your life or relationships since these feelings started, aside from your husband stopping work outside the home?
Not that I can think of. I mean, nothing big stands out besides that change at home. My relationships are mostly the same, as far as I can tell.
Do you feel like you no longer enjoy things that used to give you pleasure?
I think I answered that a bit already, but yes—my enjoyment is definitely less than it used to be. I can still do things, but they just don’t feel as satisfying or fun.
Have you experienced these symptoms for at least two years?
Yes. It’s been a little over two years—about two years and two months now. It started around when my husband stopped working outside the home and our household routine changed.
Have you ever had a period where you felt completely normal and without these gray and flat feelings for at least a couple of months?

No, I don’t think so. It’s been pretty steady for about two years and two months, since my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine changed. I can’t really point to a couple of months where I felt back to normal.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where your symptoms significantly improved?

No, not really. It’s been pretty continuous for about two years and two months, since my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine at home changed. I don’t remember a stretch of two months where it really improved.
Have you ever had a period where your symptoms got significantly better for a while, before possibly getting worse again?

No, I wouldn’t say it got significantly better at any point. It’s just been going on pretty steadily for about two years and two months, since my husband stopped working outside the home and our household routine changed.
Was there something specific that happened around the time your husband stopped working outside the home that you think might have contributed to you starting to feel this way?

I think the main thing was that change itself—when my husband stopped working outside the home, our household routine shifted. Around then is when this started, and it’s been going on for about two years and two months now.
Have your symptoms gotten worse over the two years and two months you've been experiencing them?
I’m not sure I’d say it’s gotten worse, exactly. It feels more like it’s stayed pretty steady over that time. Some days are harder than others, but I haven’t noticed a clear worsening overall.
Have you experienced these symptoms without any significant improvement for the majority of the days in the past two years?

Yes. For most days, it’s been there without any real stretch where it improved much. It’s been going on about two years and two months, since my husband stopped working outside the home and our routine changed.
Have you experienced these symptoms for at least two years without any significant periods of improvement?

Yes. It’s been about two years and two months now, and I haven’t really had any significant period where it felt better. It started around when my husband stopped working outside the home and our household routine changed.
Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you felt completely free of these gray and flat feelings?

No, I don’t think I’ve had a full two months where it was completely gone. I can get through my day and even smile with my students, but that gray, flat feeling is still there underneath most of the time. Even things I usually enjoy, like my garden or watercolors, can feel kind of distant.
